## Overview

This week is a bit of a potpourri of shorter topics,
introducing you to tools and strategies you'll use throughout the course.

You will get introduced to the Ohio Supercomputer Center (OSC),
explore best practices for project file organization,
and learn how to write Markdown files.
Along the way, you will also get to know VS Code,
a text editor you'll spend a lot of time in during this course.

## Learning goals & lectures

This week's content is divided into the following four short lectures, 
during which you will learn:

#### A) [**The Ohio Supercomputer Center (OSC)**](./w2a_osc.qmd) _(Monday)_

- What supercomputers are, and why they are useful
- What resources the Ohio Supercomputer Center (OSC) provides
- How to access OSC resources through its OnDemand webportal

#### B) [**Project organization**](./w2b_project-org.qmd) _(Monday/Wednesday)_

A number of best practices for research project...

- file organization
- file management
- documentation.

This lecture's material is available in two formats:
slides (linked to above) and a [more detailed lecture notes page](./w2b_project-org_notes.qmd).

#### C) [**VS Code**](./w2c_vscode.qmd) _(Wednesday)_

- Get to know VS Code, the text editor you'll use throughout the course.

#### D) [**Markdown**](./w2d_markdown.qmd) _(Wednesday)_

- How to use Markdown for research documentation (and beyond).

This lecture's material is available in two formats:
slides (linked to above) and a [more detailed lecture notes page](./w2d_markdown_notes.qmd).

## Readings

- [Lecture notes on project organization with some additional details](./w2b_project-org_notes.qmd)
- [Lecture notes on Markdown with some additional details](./w2d_markdown_notes.qmd)

- ["Overview of Illumina Sequencing by Synthesis Workflow"](./w1b_omics-data.html#/video-of-illumina-technology)  
  Watch this 5-minute video to learn how Illumina sequencing works.
  This is meant to provide a bit more background,
  given that the example data in this course will be from Illumina sequencing.
  This is a very quick overview and you don't need to understand all the details!

## Further resources

- [Official VS Code introductory video {{< fa external-link >}}](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/introvideos/basics){target="_blank"}\
  If you watch this, keep in mind that there are slight differences between the
  stand-alone VS Code app demonstrated in the video,
  and the VS Code _Server_ app that you run in your browser via OSC OnDemand.
  For example, there is no "Live Preview" extension for HTML files available
  for VS Code Server.

- @wilson2017: _Good enough practices in scientific computing_
